part2.intro: Three young people talk about a colourful festival they went to.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Priya
texts.text: Last March I went to the Holi festival in India with my parents. At Holi, everyone throws coloured powder and water at each other. I wore an old white T-shirt, and by lunchtime it was pink, green and yellow! It took me three days to wash the colour out of my hair. Some girls I met there taught me a traditional dance too. It was the best day of my holiday.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Tuan
texts.text: Every year my family goes to Hoi An for the Mid-Autumn Festival. The streets are full of lanterns – red, orange, purple and every other colour you can think of. My little sister and I always make our own lantern at home before we go. This year ours was a yellow star. My grandparents live in Hoi An, so we stay at their house for a week.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Sofia
texts.text: I went to a flower festival in Holland with my school. There were huge pictures made from millions of flowers, like a pink and white elephant and a red dragon. We cycled past fields of tulips, which was hard work but beautiful. I took lots of photos, and one of them is now on the wall in our classroom. The only problem was the weather – it rained all week, and the sky was always grey.

items.q: Who made something to take to the festival?
Who found it difficult to get clean after the festival?
Who stayed with family members?
Who was disappointed by the weather?
Who learned something new at the festival?
Who has something from the trip at school?
Who goes to the festival every year?

part3.title: A different way of seeing
part3.text:
When Ethan Wood was nine, his art teacher asked the class to paint a picture of a park. Ethan was happy with his picture, but when his teacher saw it, she was surprised. The grass was brown and the trees had red leaves. "I was sure I was using green," Ethan remembers.

His teacher spoke to his parents, and a doctor told them that Ethan was colour-blind. This means he can't see some colours in the same way as other people. Ethan finds it hard to see the difference between red and green, and sometimes between blue and purple. About one in twelve boys are colour-blind, but very few girls have this problem.

"Most of the time it isn't a problem," says Ethan, who is now thirteen. "But football can be difficult. Last year our team played in green shirts and the other team wore red. I kept passing the ball to the wrong players!" Now his coach always makes sure the teams wear very different colours, like white and dark blue.

For his birthday, Ethan's grandparents bought him special glasses that help colour-blind people see colours more clearly. "The first time I put them on, I looked at the garden and couldn't stop smiling. The flowers were so bright!" he says. "I don't wear them all the time, but I love using them when we go somewhere beautiful."

Ethan still loves art. "I write the names of the colours on all my pencils," he laughs. "Then I never choose the wrong one!"

items.q: How did Ethan's teacher first see that there was a problem?
options: He used unusual colours in a picture.
He didn't want to paint the park.

items.q: What does the writer say about colour-blindness?
options: It is more usual in boys than in girls.
Most colour-blind people can't see blue.

items.q: What happened when Ethan played football last year?
options: He gave the ball to the other team.
He didn't play because of his eyes.

items.q: How did Ethan feel when he first wore the special glasses?
How does Ethan make sure he uses the right colour in art?
options: He asks his teacher to help him.
He reads the words on his pencils.

part4.title: How does a rainbow happen?
part4.text:
A rainbow is one of the most beautiful things in nature. You can only see one when the sun is {19} and it is raining at the same time. The sun must be behind you, and the rain must be in front of you.

Light from the sun looks white, but it is really {20} of many colours. When sunlight goes through raindrops, it breaks into different colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. Red is always at the top of a rainbow, and purple is always at the {21}.

Sometimes you can see two rainbows at the same time. The second one is lighter, and its colours are in the {22} order – red is at the bottom!

In many countries there are old stories about rainbows. In Ireland, people say there is a pot of gold at the end of a rainbow. But nobody has ever found it, because you can never {23} the end of a rainbow – it moves when you move! If you want to {24} a photo of one, be quick, because most rainbows only last a few minutes.

part7.instruction: Look at the three pictures. Write the story shown in the pictures. Write 35 words or more.

pictures.caption: a boy putting his white football shirt into the washing machine; a red sock is inside too
the boy holding up his football shirt, which is now pink; he looks shocked
the boy in the pink shirt scores a goal and his team are cheering

part7.model: On Friday evening Tom washed his white football shirt for the match. He didn't see that one of his red socks was in the machine too. When he took the shirt out, it was pink! Tom was very unhappy. But the next day he wore it to the match and scored the winning goal. Now it's his lucky shirt!

items.q: Which car is Dad's new car?

script.t: Have you seen Dad's new car? It's outside.
Is it that red one?
No, that's Mrs Taylor's. Dad's is the grey one next to it.
Grey? He always said he wanted a white car.
He did, but the white one was more expensive.

items.q: Which flowers does the boy buy for his grandmother?

script.t: I'd like some flowers for my grandma, please. She loves yellow ones.
Sorry, we haven't got any yellow ones today. But these pink roses are lovely.
Hmm, her garden's already full of pink roses. What about those purple ones?
They're five pounds.
Perfect. I'll take them.

items.q: Which girl is Hannah?

script.t: Which one is your sister Hannah? The girl with light hair?
No, that's my cousin. Hannah's got dark hair, like me.
Is she the one in the blue dress?
No, that's her friend. Hannah's wearing green. It's her favourite colour.

items.q: Which bird did the girl see in the garden?

script.t: Dad, there was a beautiful bird in the garden this morning.
Was it a robin? They've got a red front.
No, it was small and blue, with a yellow front.
Ah, that's a blue tit. We often see blackbirds here, but blue tits don't come very often.

items.q: Which pencil case does the boy choose?

script.t: Look at these pencil cases, Sam. This pink one's lovely.
My sister's got that one. I want something different.
What about black? It won't look dirty.
Black's so boring. I'll get the orange one. Then nobody will take it by mistake!

part2.intro: You will hear a man talking on the radio about a summer painting course for young people.
part2.title: Summer Painting Course

items.label: In the first week, students paint:
Bring these paints: blue, yellow and

script.t: Are you between eleven and fifteen? Do you love colours? Then come to our summer painting course! The course runs from Monday to Thursday every week in August. We used to have classes on Fridays too, but now that's the day we clean the studio! In the first week, we'll go down to the harbour and paint the boats. They're all different colours – red, blue, green and orange – so it's a great place to start. In the second week, we'll paint the flowers in the city park. The course costs forty-five pounds a week for students. Adults can join too, but they pay sixty pounds. We'll give you brushes, paper and some paints – we've got lots of red, black and brown. But please bring your own blue, yellow and white, because we always run out of those colours. And wear old clothes, of course! Your teacher will be Mrs Fenton. That's F-E-N-T-O-N. She's a well-known artist, and her paintings of the sea are in lots of galleries. We hope to see you there!

part3.intro: You will hear Mia talking to her grandfather about her holiday in Iceland.

items.q: On which night did Mia see the northern lights?
What colour were the lights mostly?
Why didn't Mia take any good photos?
What was unusual about the beaches?
What did Mia buy for her grandfather?

script.t: Welcome back, Mia! How was Iceland?
Amazing, Grandpa! It was really cold, but I loved it.
Did you see the northern lights?

Yes! We tried on the first night, but it was too cloudy. On the second night we were too tired after a long walk, so we went to bed early. But on the third night the sky was clear, and suddenly there they were!
What colours were they? I've seen photos with pink and purple lights.
Sometimes they're pink, but ours were mostly green – bright green, moving across the dark sky like a river. There was a little bit of purple at the end.
Did you take any photos?
I tried, but my phone wasn't good enough – all my photos were just black! Luckily Dad had his big camera, so he got some great ones.
And what else did you do?
We swam in a hot pool outside, even when it was snowing. And we walked on some beaches where the sand is black, because of the volcanoes. It looked so strange!
Did you bring me anything?
Of course! I wanted to get you a sweater, but they were really expensive. So I got you this grey and white hat instead.
Lovely, thank you! Will you go back one day?
I hope so. Mum says next time we'll go in summer, when it's light nearly all night. But you can't see the northern lights then.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her father about a school project.
items.q: What does she need help with?
options: choosing a colour for a poster

script.t: Dad, can you help me with my geography project? It's a poster about flags of the world.
Sure. Do you need help finding information?
No, I've done that, and I've drawn all the flags. But I can't decide on the background. White looks boring, and black is too dark.
What about light blue, like the sky?

items.q: Why is he calling?
options: to say he will be late
to ask what he should wear

script.t: Hi Ana, it's Kevin. I'm at the concert already – I got here early. It's really busy, so it won't be easy to find me. I'm near the front, next to the big speaker on the left, and I'm wearing my orange cap. So look for orange! Text me when you arrive.

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a new café.
items.q: What does the girl think about the café?

script.t: Have you been to the new café in the square?
Yes, last weekend. The cakes are really good, and they aren't expensive.
It's quite small, isn't it?
There's enough space. But the walls are bright red and the chairs are bright yellow – it hurts my eyes! I couldn't relax at all.

items.intro: You will hear a teacher talking to her class in a science lesson.
items.q: What will the students do today?

script.t: Last week we watched a video about light and colour. Today you're going to do an experiment. Each group has three small bottles of water – red, yellow and blue. Mix them and see what new colours you can make. Can you make green? Orange? Purple? Write everything in your book. Next week we'll try to make our own rainbow with a glass of water and a torch.

items.intro: You will hear a man talking about his job.
items.q: What is his job?

script.t: In my job, I talk to people about colour all the time. Lots of people want white walls in every room, but I try to help them choose something more exciting – a light green for a bedroom, maybe, or a warm orange for a kitchen. I'm not an artist, and I don't paint pictures. I just make people's homes look beautiful. I can usually finish one room in two days.

part5.intro: You will hear Jack talking to his friend Emma about a school art competition. What did each student paint?

script.t: Jack, have you seen the paintings for the art competition? They're all in the hall now.
Yes! Ruby's is amazing. At first I thought it was a big pink flower, but it's a flamingo standing in a lake.
Oh yes, Ruby loves birds. What did Daniel paint? He said he was going to do a horse.
He wanted to, but he said horses are too difficult to draw. So he did a big grey elephant instead. It's really good.
And Kai? He always paints the sea.
Not this time. He painted a green frog sitting on a leaf. It's very funny – it's got huge eyes.
What about Lucy? Did she paint her cat?
No. Her cat's black, and she says black paint looks too dark on paper. So she painted the yellow sun going down over the hills behind her house. The sky's orange and pink.
Lovely. And yours? You haven't told me!
Mine's a white boat on a dark blue sea. I wanted to put an orange fish in the water under the boat, but I didn't have enough time.
Well, I think you'll win!
